access_notes.value: API access is tied to a Zendesk user account: API-token requests must present the email address of an admin, agent, or other valid user, and OAuth tokens are bound to the user who authorized the app. The marketing site advertises a free trial ('Try it for free') and pricing lists paid per-agent plans from $19/agent/month; whether the trial includes API credentials is not stated in the fetched pages. Sandbox environments appear only in the top-tier feature list.
access_notes.quote: However, you must provide an email address for an admin, agent, or other valid user when authenticating requests.

official_mcp_server.quote: In your external agent's AI platform, connect your external AI agent to Zendesk with an MCP server URL specified in the connection you configured.

verdict_reason: Zendesk documents a broad developer platform - APIs for ticketing, help center, live chat, voice, sales CRM, omnichannel routing and custom data - with OAuth 2.0 and API-token authentication, documented scopes, a public Postman collection, and published per-plan rate limits. The lowest-friction documented route to credentials is self-serve: the site advertises a free trial ('Try it for free'), with paid per-agent plans from $19/agent/month for production. No partner approval, app review, or sales contact is required, so the toolkit is buildable at low friction, with the paid production plan as the only commercial gate.
open_questions: No fetched page explicitly labels the Zendesk API 'REST'; api_type is inferred from documented HTTP-method JSON endpoints under /api/v2, hence confidence=medium.

Whether the advertised free trial ('Try it for free') includes API credentials, and for how long, is not documented in the bundle; if it does not, access_model would revert to paid_plan_required and the verdict to moderate.
No numeric endpoint/resource count for the full API surface was found on the fetched pages, so api_breadth carries no count.
The webhooks/event-types page was listed in the bundle's audit sources but its text was not included in SOURCES, so webhooks support could not be cited verbatim.

API versioning/deprecation pages were not included in SOURCES; the API-token sunset dates appeared only in search snippets (unused tokens deactivating 2026-07-28, all API tokens stopping 2027-04-30) and could not be quoted.

The Zendesk MCP server endpoint is per-org and only generated per configured connection; Zendesk Bridge / external AI agents are in an early access program (EAP), so GA packaging and pricing are unknown.
Only client-side SDKs (Android, iOS, Unity, Web Widget) are evidenced in the fetched docs; no official server-side API client libraries were found in the bundle.

Rate limits cited here cover only the plan-based per-minute table; the same page also documents endpoint-specific limits (e.g., Update Ticket 30 per 10 min per user per ticket, Incremental Exports 10 req/min) and 429/Retry-After behaviour, which could not fit into one verbatim quote.
